value.body: State Information and Public Relations departments handle government communication: press releases, media relations, government advertising, publications, social media and publicity for schemes. Posts include Assistant or Deputy Director and District Information and Public Relations Officer, plus assistant-level information posts.

items.label: Recruiting bodies
items.value: State PSCs or state staff selection boards

items.label: Typical qualification
items.value: Degree with journalism, mass communication or PR

items.label: B.J.M.C. students
items.note: Bachelor of Journalism and Mass Communication only; mass communication is also taught under other degree names

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Typically a bachelor's degree with a degree or diploma in journalism, mass communication or public relations; some posts also ask for media experience and knowledge of the state language. Recruitment is through the state Public Service Commission or staff selection board, with a written exam and/or interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: Knowledge of the state's official language is usually essential.
Work follows government events and deadlines, including evenings and holidays.
The central counterpart, the Indian Information Service, recruits through UPSC and SSC.

value.title: B.J.M.C. enrolment
value.note: Counts only the B.J.M.C. programme name; B.J., B.A. (Journalism) and similar degrees are listed separately. Pool of graduates, not government posts.
value.source: AISHE reports 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), programme-wise enrolment table — B.J.M.C., all modes
